en.name: Plateau pressure (Pplat)
en.shortDescription: Plateau pressure (Pplat) — airway pressure during an end-inspiratory hold, in cmH2O.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Plateau pressure (Pplat) is the airway pressure at zero inspiratory flow, reflecting the pressure distending the alveoli — the elastic recoil of the lungs and chest wall. It is a key target in lung-protective ventilation (kept ≤ ~30 cmH2O). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar). The zero-flow condition is usually obtained with an end-inspiratory hold, but not always: in pressure-control modes where inspiratory flow decelerates to zero before the end of inspiration, the end-inspiratory pressure already is the plateau, and some ventilator pneumatics cannot perform a hold at all and derive the value instead. ## Included Concepts The set resolves to six concepts: five LOINC "Clinical Observation" codes and one SNOMED observable entity. - *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway (LOINC)*: the generic LOINC plateau pressure, context unspecified. The default. - *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same measurement, with the "on ventilator" context made explicit. - *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure (SNOMED)*: the SNOMED equivalent, for sources that carry no LOINC code. - *3006369 / 20060-0 — Airway pressure --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same quantity named after its defining condition rather than after "plateau". This is the framing the German Medical Informatics Initiative core dataset uses for plateau pressure. - *3012810 / 20059-2 — Airway pressure by Airway pressure monitor --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same code with the measuring device made explicit. - *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure (LOINC)*: a plateau pressure obtained without a dedicated hold manoeuvre — see below. The two `Pressure.plateau` LOINC codes are pulled in through their shared LOINC Hierarchy anchor, which covers exactly these two and nothing else. The other three LOINC codes sit on separate branches and are listed explicitly — in particular, the `Pressure.airway` anchor is deliberately **not** used, since it also covers peak and mean airway pressures, which are different measurands. **Note on the "dynamic" concept.** LOINC publishes no definition for *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure*, and its component (`Pressure.plateau dynamic`) differs from the `Pressure.plateau` component of the two codes above. Its meaning comes from IEEE 11073-10101, of which it is an import: the code maps as `equivalent` to `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` (152776) in the LOINC/IEEE mapping table shipped with the LOINC release [1], where the term denotes the airway pressure that would have been observed during an inspiratory hold — a plateau obtained without performing one. Valveless ventilators do this by necessity: the HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 derive it as `(VTE / Cstat) + PEEP` and display it only when end-inspiratory flow is near zero [2]. All six concepts therefore describe the same physiological quantity and share the same unit, which is why they are kept in one set; what differs is how the zero-flow condition was reached, and how the source vocabulary chose to name it. **Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a plateau pressure (Pplat): *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway*. This is the generic LOINC code, and the one ventilators emit through the IEEE 11073 Rosetta respiratory panel. - **Source states the patient was on the ventilator**: *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator*. - **Source carries no LOINC code**: *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure* (SNOMED). - **Source names the value after the zero-flow condition** rather than after "plateau" — as the German MII core dataset does: *3006369 / 20060-0 — Airway pressure --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator*, or *3012810 / 20059-2 — Airway pressure by Airway pressure monitor --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator* when the measuring device is stated. - **Use *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure* only** when the source explicitly labels the value as obtained without a hold manoeuvre — a device field named for a dynamic or estimated plateau, or a ventilator model known not to perform holds. A plateau pressure of unknown provenance is **not** a reason to pick it: use the generic code above. - The six concepts belong in the same column. Where the distinction matters for an analysis — comparing a hold-derived value with a device-derived one — recover it from `measurement_concept_id`, not from the value. - Convert mbar to cmH2O (×1.02) before mapping. - **Not peak, mean or PEEP**: these are distinct pressures in their own concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC/IEEE Medical Device Code Mapping Table, distributed with the LOINC release (`AccessoryFiles/LoincIeeeMedicalDeviceCodeMappingTable`). Maps LOINC 60802-6 to IEEE 11073-10101 `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` (152776) as `equivalent`. Available: https://loinc.org/downloads/ [2] Hamilton Medical. Calculating Pplateau with HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 ventilators. Available: https://www.hamilton-medical.com/en_US/Resource-center/Article-page~knowledge-base~14232908-6f10-47d0-abe1-2e5b9de333f1~Calculating-Pplateau-with-HAMILTON-C1-T1-MR1-ventilators~.html

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Add four LOINC concepts, as suggested in issue #23: the two Pressure.plateau codes (60829-9, 76259-1) via their LOINC Hierarchy anchor, and the two Pressure.airway^at zero inspiratory flow codes (20060-0, 20059-2), the framing the German MII core dataset uses. Make 60829-9 the default and document Dynamic plateau pressure from its IEEE 11073 source term. Resolves to 6 standard concepts.
